context.axis: is the binding law's own quantity extensive, and is that good news at A <= 4?
context.answer: It is extensive — Delta_tr/A has 6.7 % relative spread, 26x flatter than B/A — and that is exactly the obstruction. B/A moves 6.4x over the same four atoms, so the per-nucleon deficit runs 5.1 to 32.3 and is not a constant. No fixed multiple of an extensive quantity closes it.
context.bearing_on_prior_work: qou-imcd's exponent measurement and qou-78pt's shape claim are not disputed; both measure the NORMALISER. The addition is the same measurement on the binding law's own quantity, plus the observation that all four calibration atoms sit far below the B/A plateau, so extensivity cannot be assessed on them.
context.open_for_owner: The normaliser route and the binding law give 1.2309 and 0.2253 MeV/nucleon for what both are presented as — the framework's extensive energy per nucleon. They are different objects with different scales, so this need not be an error, but they cannot both be the prediction.
